topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer genetics
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning objectives and connects prior practical histopathology observations to the cellular and genetic mechanisms of cancer.

topics.label: Tumor virology and experimental assays for cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical investigation of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental assays to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Genetic characteristics and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classifications of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes and illustrate their genetic behaviors through cell cycle control and dominant-negative mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms and multi-step progression of genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate genetic instability and drive multi-step tumor development.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how inherited germline mutations in gatekeeper and caretaker genes accelerate cancer onset and influence ongoing tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with reading recommendations and administrative framing for the next lecture.
